items.note: The shop's whole premise: vegetables puréed into the dough rather than laid on top, so the loaf itself comes out green or orange. Komatsuna (mustard spinach) and carrot versions are standard, and there is a spinach one. Still wheat bread — the vegetables change the colour and the sweetness, not the gluten. The bakery is run as a supported-employment workshop by the Ms-Net non-profit.
Sliced orange right through. Also made with spinach.
¥310–¥360. Add ¥300–¥350 for a mini salad and a drink. Fillings seen: steamed chicken with kinpira burdock, greens and egg, potato salad, carrot and Spam, keema curry.

items.ja: まるパンサンド（3個セット）
items.note: The shop's own announcement: three of the popular vegetable rolls with different fillings — salmon and onion, fluffy egg, burdock salad in one set; salmon, anko-butter and burdock in the other.
Panko-crumbed patty; the sauce is wheat-based too.
The shop's own note says roughly ¥500–¥610 depending on what goes in: a sandwich or roll-sandwich plus sides and a cake. Contents change daily and you choose the box at the counter.

Named by the shop as its most popular rice dish: rice under a soft omelette with the house hayashi sauce poured over. Comes with a mini salad. Add ¥200–¥250 for a drink set including coffee, tea, Nara cider, minestrone or juice. Hayashi sauce is a wheat roux.
¥1,000 with a ¥200 coffee.

items.ja: ごはんランチ「キーマカレー」
items.note: Balanced meat and vegetable; served with a vegetable-noodle carrot salad. Japanese curry base is a wheat roux.

items.ja: ミニサラダ（にんじんと玉ネギのマリネ）
items.romaji: mini sarada — ninjin to tamanegi no marine
items.en: Mini salad: carrot and onion marinade
items.note: One of three that are out every Tuesday to Friday. Sweet vegetables against a gentle vinegar.

items.ja: オリジナルポテトサラダ
items.note: Chunky and rich. Japanese mayonnaise contains egg.

items.ja: ひじきとキャベツのサラダ
items.note: With the shop's own dressing.
Vegetable-heavy but contains pork.

items.ja: トマトの煮込みハンバーグバーガー

items.note: A seasonal announcement from the shop.
Valentine's only, sold as a two-piece set: chocolate with milk-chocolate chips and strawberry with white-chocolate chips.
Run occasionally rather than daily — check before going.

items.en: Set A — welcome drink, coffee roasted to your taste, and a sweets plate
items.note: The cafe is reservation-only, one party of up to four per slot, ninety minutes, booked by the previous noon. The coffee is roasted for you after you order — say what you like and they roast to it — and refills are included. Note the shop's site has been flagged 'under maintenance' since February 2026, so confirm before travelling.

items.en: Set B — coffee roasted to your taste with a raw cake
items.note: Same coffee, one raw cake instead of the full plate. Refills included.

This is the reason to come and the reason to ask questions. The shop's own description of raw sweets: no egg, no dairy, no wheat flour and no white sugar, nothing heated above 48°C, built from fresh and dried fruit and soaked nuts. That makes them plausibly wheat-free and often dairy-free — but the shop makes no allergen declaration and shares a small kitchen, and some raw recipes use honey. Ask about the specific cake.

items.ja: ローチーズケーキタルト
items.note: 'Cheese' here means blended soaked cashews, not dairy; the base is nuts and dates rather than biscuit. From the shop's own teaching syllabus.
Cacao worked without roasting. A white-chocolate version is made too.
Dates, nuts and cacao pressed rather than baked.
Dried fruit and nuts rolled into bite-size balls.
Green beans from around the world, hand-roasted; the shop also teaches hand-roasting classes. Refills come with both sets.
A raw-food take on the Sichuan noodle — vegetable 'noodles' with a nut-and-sesame sauce, nothing cooked. Lunch is not always available; ask when booking.

items.ja: ローツナマヨ海苔巻き
items.note: The tuna and the mayonnaise are both plant-based reconstructions.
A jun-kissa built around a serious hi-fi system that dominates the middle of the room. Coffee is served by origin.
Reported ¥550–¥650; the shop sometimes knocks ¥50 off as the day's special.
The house everyday cup.
Recommended by regulars alongside a charcoal-roasted option.
Roasting over binchotan charcoal rather than gas gives a rounder, smokier cup.
Reviewers note the shop imports the real thing rather than a domestic blend.
Reported ¥400 in 2017 and ¥500 more recently. Gelatin-set on a biscuit base.
Price is from 2016. Thick-cut and simple — the whole food menu here is essentially toast.

The thing to eat here, and the farm says so itself. Made from that morning's milk, on the oldest working dairy farm in Nara prefecture, right beside Hannya-ji temple. Sold only at the farm shop — the restaurant does not serve it. The shop closes for winter, early December to mid-March.

Low-temperature pasteurised — 75°C for fifteen minutes, the old way — and 100% raw milk with nothing added. The farm still delivers 700–800 bottles a day to houses nearby, and supplies the Nara Hotel. The taste genuinely varies day to day because the cows are fed whatever vegetables the neighbouring farms send over.
Same glass bottle, same recipe as when the farm opened in the Meiji era.

items.ja: 植村牧場特製 牛乳もなか
items.note: Milk ice cream between crisp wafers. The round version has been discontinued. Monaka wafers are usually mochi rice — ask.

The standard: soup (a chilled pumpkin soup on one visit), salad, bread (baguette and a fig loaf) and a main such as hamburg steak in tomato sauce. The chef trained at the Nara Hotel. Bread and demi-glace both mean wheat.
The Ichizu lunch plus a drink and dessert — and the drink can be the farm's own fresh milk. A three-meat version has been served.
Mixed fried items with rice; reported ¥1,300–¥1,400. Panko is wheat.
The cheapest way in.

items.ja: 海老クリームコロッケ
items.note: Thin crumb around a milk-heavy béchamel that runs when you cut it — the farm's own milk is the point. Flour roux plus panko.
Chicken rice wrapped in a barely-set omelette; a long-running favourite here.
Slow-cooked beef in a curry lightened with the farm's milk, giving it a yoghurt-like tang. Japanese curry roux is wheat.
Winter only, made with the farm's milk. A doria version also exists.
Fillet pork with pork-and-miso soup and pickles.

items.ja: いちづ特製アップルパイ（ホール）
items.note: A whole pie packed with apple, sold to take away. The farm suggests warming it in a toaster oven.

items.ja: スイーツセット（珈琲付）
items.note: The cafe menu runs from 2pm.
Can be taken instead of the post-meal coffee in a set.

The entry lunch, tax included. Twelve seats, counter and private rooms, one Michelin star. The menu changes month by month with the market. Kaiseki is built on soy and dashi, so gluten and fish are unavoidable without a long conversation in advance.
Service charge additional.
The same course as dinner, at lunch. Service charge additional. Three lunch courses are offered in total.
A single dinner course, tax included, service charge additional.

items.en: The dashi — southern Hokkaido ma-kombu and aged katsuobushi
items.note: The restaurant names this as the foundation of everything it serves: a generous quantity of premium ma-kombu for depth, with hon-karebushi — bonito dried, smoked and mould-cured over months — from which the dark bloodline has been trimmed away so the stock stays clean. Bonito means no kaiseki course here can be made vegan.

Nara prefecture formally designates a list of traditional local vegetables as Yamato-yasai — among them Yamato-mana greens, the round Yamato-marunasu aubergine, Katahira akane radish and Uda-kin burdock. The kitchen builds seasonal dishes around whatever is in.

Kaiseki was originally food designed to be drunk with, and the restaurant states plainly that each dish is built to complement the sake rather than the other way round. You can choose your own ochoko cup.

items.ja: 焼酎・シャンパン・ワイン・ウイスキー
items.note: Whisky is barley; wine is often animal-fined. You may pick your own glass.

The house loaf, and the price has held remarkably steady — ¥250 for a slab, about ¥310 a full kin. Note there is an unrelated shop in Naramachi also called Kohaku (七福食堂／喫茶古白) — this one is the bakery near Ichijo High School north of Shin-Omiya.
The custard is injected at the till after you pay, and the shop tells you to eat it immediately — the shell is still crisp and the custard still cool for about two minutes.
The standard version of the above, also filled to order.
Also sold as a tea-and-lemon cream bun at ¥160 + tax.

The bagels are the shop's obsession — dense, tightly packed and heavily filled. Filled versions include shiso, roast ham and mozzarella; perilla with cheese; cheese dakgalbi; and Chinese chive with ham.
Made with Omi beef, one of Japan's three great wagyu. Medium heat. A curry frankfurter version is ¥292 including tax; a plain curry pan ¥190.

items.ja: さとうきびのでにっしゅ
items.note: Made with unrefined cane sugar.
Black soybeans from Uda, the highland district east of Nara city.

items.ja: 小豆入あんことれんにゅう
items.note: Whole azuki beans left in the paste.

items.ja: パレード！カンパーニュ
items.note: The shop runs many campagne variants: fig and walnut; cranberry, orange and cream cheese; tea, raisin and cream cheese; blueberry and cream cheese.

items.ja: ワイルドブルーベリーと紅茶 アーモンドとクリームチーズ
items.romaji: wairudo buruuberii to koucha aamondo to kuriimu chiizu
items.en: Wild blueberry, tea, almond and cream cheese

items.note: Snipped and splayed so the loaf comes out shaped like an ear of wheat; you tear the pieces off. Repeatedly named the shop's best item.

items.ja: スモークサーモンの野菜たっぷりサンド
items.romaji: sumooku saamon no yasai tappuri sando
items.en: Smoked salmon sandwich with a lot of vegetables
items.note: Price is from a 2013 report.

items.ja: サーモンとチーズフォンデュデニッシュ
アボカドとソーセージのタコスミート
items.romaji: abokado to sooseeji no takosu miito

items.ja: いちごとクリームチーズのマフィン
items.romaji: ichigo to kuriimu chiizu no mafin
items.note: Price before tax.
Autumn. A candied-chestnut cream version also appears.
Price from an old listing and long out of date; a petit-france is also sold.
